Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year, which runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split that between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

From 6 April 2027, investors under 65 will be able to pay no more than £12,000 a year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance stays the same.

More detail is in our ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000. That applies to adults aged 18 or over, and the tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

You can split the £20,000 between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The documents I have only talk about ISAs for adults aged 18 or over. They don't say whether a 17-year-old can open an ISA with us, so I can't confirm it either way. They also don't cover any ISA for under-18s.

The Lifetime ISA is open to people aged 18 to 39. Your daughter would have to wait until she's 18 for that one. For a definite answer about her age, please call our switchboard or speak to your adviser.

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

You can open a Lifetime ISA if you're aged 18 to 39. Withdrawals for reasons other than the permitted ones incur a 25% government charge. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes. According to our ISA guide, a Lifetime ISA can only be opened by people aged 18 to 39, so at 42 you can't open one.

I can't tell you what to do instead, because that would be advice. If you'd like to talk through other options, I can pass your question to an adviser. Our ISA guide is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The guide lists these changes from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay no more than £12,000 into cash ISAs each tax year. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance doesn't change. The rest can go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- You will no longer be able to transfer from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own ISAs. If you want that, I can pass you to an adviser.

From 6 April 2027, the cash ISA cap is £12,000 a year for investors under 65. At 70, you're in the group that keeps a £20,000 cash ISA limit, so the cap doesn't apply to you. Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap either.

Two other changes from that date: transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted. A charge will also apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, transfers between cash ISAs should take no longer than 15 working days. Other ISA transfers should take no longer than 30 calendar days. Re-registering holdings in specie (moving them as they are) can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

The receiving provider starts the transfer. You should do it through their transfer process and not by withdrawing the money, so the ISA keeps its tax status. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. Money you withdraw during a tax year can be replaced in the same tax year without using more of your allowance.

The 2026/27 tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. Unused allowance doesn't carry forward. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes, in effect. A surviving spouse or civil partner is entitled to an additional permitted subscription equal to the value of the deceased's ISAs. This is on top of their own allowance. It applies whether or not they inherit the investments themselves.

The ISA also stays tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/ and the full address ends with the final slash.

The pension annual allowance is £60,000. This counts the total paid into your pensions in a tax year, including employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual. If you go over it, an annual allowance charge is normally due.

- **Tapering:** For high earners, the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on how this applies to your own situation. For that, please raise it with an adviser.

Yes, you can still pay in, but a lower limit applies. Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

The documents don't say how this applies to your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser. More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Normally, you can take up to 25% of a pension tax free. This is subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above that allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't tell you how much you should take or when. If you want advice on your own situation, I can pass your question to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise. We will also offer to book a free guidance appointment for you, as the rules require. We won't do this if you have already had one or have received regulated advice.

More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on which option is right for you. If you want that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest.

The documents don't say what applies to transfer values of £30,000 or less. If that's your situation, raise it with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will be included in the value of your estate for inheritance tax. Before that date, the documents I have don't say how pensions are treated.

Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, remain exempt. Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.

Income tax is a separate matter. If you die before age 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

I can't advise on your own circumstances. Please raise those with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. Your own contributions get tax relief up to 100% of your relevant UK earnings in the tax year, or £3,600 gross if your earnings are lower. With no earnings, the £3,600 gross figure is the one that applies. Basic-rate relief is added to the pension automatically.

You can read more in our pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't tell you whether you should pay in or how much. If you'd like advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Yes. Unused annual allowance from the previous three tax years can be carried forward, provided you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.

The annual allowance is £60,000. For high earners it tapers down to a minimum of £10,000. The documents don't say how much you could carry forward in your own case. For that, please raise it with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

A full financial plan costs £2,400, plus VAT where it applies. It covers a review of your whole financial position, a written plan with recommendations, and a meeting to go through it.

One-off advice on a single topic costs £1,200, plus VAT where it applies. An example is how to use allowances before the end of the tax year. Financial planning is available at any level of wealth.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Ongoing advice costs 0.75% a year of the assets under advice, collected monthly from your accounts. It covers your annual review meeting, access to your adviser throughout the year, rebalancing recommendations and the quarterly reports.

If you also have discretionary investment management, that fee applies as well. Your client agreement sets out the combined cost. Your annual costs and charges statement shows it in pounds.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

For a £2m portfolio, the tiered annual discretionary management fee is:

- 0.60% a year on the first £1,000,000.
- 0.45% a year on the portion between £1,000,000 and £3,000,000, which covers the second £1,000,000 of your portfolio.

VAT is added to the fee. If you also receive ongoing advice, both fees apply. The combined cost is set out in your client agreement and shown in pounds in your annual costs and charges statement.

The fee schedule is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

It depends on the account type:

- **Model portfolios:** there are no dealing charges. That includes when holdings are sold to pay a withdrawal or to close an account.
- **Advisory accounts:** individual share trades cost £12.50 each.

Custody of your assets by our custodian costs 0.15% a year. Fund charges are separate and are deducted within the funds.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

It depends on the service:

- Advice that leads to us arranging a product or investment for you is exempt from VAT.
- Stand-alone advice and discretionary investment management are subject to VAT at the standard rate.

Your client agreement states which of your fees carry VAT. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

No. We're paid by fees agreed with you in advance, and we don't receive commission from product providers. Your client agreement and services and costs disclosure confirm all fees in writing before any work starts.

You can see our standard rates on the Fees and Charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Our discretionary investment management service is designed for portfolios of £250,000 or more. Financial planning is available at any level of wealth.

More detail is on the Fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

No, there's no charge for closing an account or for transferring out.

If holdings have to be sold on our model portfolios, there are no dealing charges. Fund charges continue to be deducted within the funds until the holdings are transferred or sold.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The funds carry their own charges on top of our fee. The fund managers set these charges, and they are deducted within the fund. Across our model portfolios, the average ongoing fund charge was 0.21% a year at 30 June 2026.

Each April we send every client a statement. It shows in pounds all the charges paid in the previous year, including fund charges. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

You can complain by letter, telephone, email or in person, and you can raise it with anyone in the firm. The Client Resolution team can be reached:
- Email: complaints@fernhillwealth.example
- Telephone: 0117 496 0355, 09:00 to 17:30 on working days
- Post: Client Resolution, Fernhill Wealth, Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY

There is no charge for complaining, and it won't affect the service you receive. If someone is complaining for you, we need your written permission before we can discuss your affairs with them.

After you complain, we either confirm a resolution in writing if we can settle it within three working days, or acknowledge it in writing within five working days and tell you who is handling it. More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

The documents give these timings:

- If we can resolve your complaint within three working days, we confirm it in a summary resolution letter.
- Otherwise we acknowledge your complaint in writing within five working days and tell you who is handling it.
- If the investigation can't be completed within eight weeks of receiving your complaint, we write to explain the delay. That letter says when we expect to respond and explains your right to go to the Financial Ombudsman Service without waiting.

If you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one, you can refer the matter free of charge to the Financial Ombudsman Service. You must do this within six months of the date of our final response. More detail is on our complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

If you're unhappy with our final response, you can refer the matter free of charge to the Financial Ombudsman Service. You must do this within six months of the date of our final response.

- Telephone: 0800 023 4567, or 0300 123 9123
- Website: www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk
- Post: Financial Ombudsman Service, Exchange Tower, London, E14 9SR

You can also contact our Client Resolution team on 0117 496 0355 (09:00 to 17:30 on working days) or at complaints@fernhillwealth.example. More detail is on our complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

The Financial Ombudsman Service's telephone numbers are 0800 023 4567 and 0300 123 9123.

You can refer a complaint to them free of charge if you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one. You must do this within six months of the date of our final response.

Their website is www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk.

It may not be too late. The Ombudsman can normally consider a complaint made within six years of the event. It can also consider one made within three years of when you became aware, or should reasonably have become aware, that you had cause to complain. Whichever of those is later applies. Four years is inside the six-year period.

If you aren't sure whether your complaint is in time, contact us anyway. More details are on the complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

If you want to raise the complaint now, tell me and I'll pass it to our Client Resolution team.

Yes. Our Manchester office is at Suite 3, Peterloo Buildings, 41 Mosley Street, Manchester, M2 3ZX. The telephone number is 0161 496 0170, and the nearest tram stop is St Peter's Square.

The office has step-free access and accessible toilets. There is a hearing loop in the meeting rooms. Advisers there are also available for telephone and video meetings.

Our head office is in Bristol: Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY. The telephone number is 0117 496 0100.

It's a short walk from Temple Meads station. The nearest car park is Harbourside Multi-Storey.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Our London office is at Fourth Floor, 18 Moorgate Court, London, EC2R 6ZX. The nearest stations are Moorgate and Bank. You can phone the office on 020 7946 0150.

More details are on our contact page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/
The main switchboard (0117 496 0100) is open 08:30 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays.

No. Our offices are closed at weekends, so you can't visit on a Sunday. They're open 09:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday, and closed on bank holidays. Visits are by appointment so that the right adviser is available for you.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Yes. The new client enquiries line is 0808 157 0450. It's free from UK landlines and mobiles. It's open 09:00 to 17:30 on working days unless stated otherwise.

You can also use that number to book a free introductory appointment. The meeting lasts about 45 minutes and carries no charge and no obligation.

Please address post to: Fernhill Wealth, Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY. Mark the envelope for the attention of your adviser or the relevant team.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Yes, we have an office in Edinburgh. It's at 12 Charlotte Lane, Edinburgh, EH2 4ZX, five minutes from Haymarket station. The telephone number is 0131 496 0160.

Advisers at every office are also available for telephone and video meetings. More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Use the "Forgotten password" link on the login page. We email a reset link to the address we hold, and the link is valid for 30 minutes.

If your account is locked, it stays locked for 30 minutes after five incorrect attempts. If you're still locked out after that, call the portal access helpline on 0117 496 0233. It's open 09:00 to 17:30 on working days.

More details: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

Five incorrect login attempts lock the account for 30 minutes. If you're still locked out after that, call the portal access helpline on 0117 496 0233. It's open 09:00 to 17:30 on working days.

Other things to try:
- **Forgotten password:** use the Forgotten password link on the login page. A reset link is emailed to the address we hold and is valid for 30 minutes.
- **No verification code:** check that your phone has signal, or use the backup codes issued when you set up two-step verification.
- **Changed phone number:** call the helpline so we can re-register your device. We'll ask you to confirm your identity.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

No, two-step verification can't be switched off. You log in with your email address, your password and a six-digit code. The code comes from your authenticator app or is sent by text message.

You can read more on the client portal page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

You can see transactions for the last seven years in the client portal.

More details are on the portal page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

The documents say secure messages to and from your adviser get "a reply within two working days". They don't say anything more about response times.

You can find this on the client portal page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

You can change your address in the client portal under My Details, or by secure message.

If you'd rather write to us, the postal address is Fernhill Wealth, Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY. Mark the envelope for the attention of your adviser or the relevant team.

To change your name after marriage, we need a certified copy of your marriage or civil partnership certificate. A deed poll also works. Either way, we need your birth certificate with it.

The documents I found don't say how to send them. For that, you could use a secure message in the client portal, or call the switchboard.

For a general investment account or ISA:

- **Cash already available:** we pay within five working days of your instruction.
- **Holdings have to be sold first:** sales normally settle within two working days of dealing. We then pay within five working days of settlement.

Pension withdrawals depend on your age and the type of pension. Tax may be payable. The Pensions page explains the options.

If you want to make a withdrawal, I can pass your instruction to a person.

Valuation reports are issued quarterly. They come out within 15 working days of the end of March, June, September and December. They're published to the client portal.

You can also ask your adviser's team for a valuation as at any date. It's normally available within two working days.

To change the bank account we pay withdrawals to, you need to give us two things:
- a signed instruction
- a recent statement for the new account that shows your name

We then confirm the change with you by telephone, on the number we hold, before it takes effect. Withdrawals are paid only to a bank account in your name that we have verified in this way.

The documents don't say how to send us the signed instruction and statement. The client support page is https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/

Yes. Paper copies by post can be arranged at no extra charge. Ask your adviser's team to set it up. All documents are still published to the portal as well.

More detail is on the client support page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/

Yes. Interest is paid on cash balances at the rates shown on the portal. We keep a margin of 0.25% a year between the rate we receive and the rate we pay. Your client agreement discloses this margin.

Interest on cash outside an ISA or pension is taxable. It's reported on your annual consolidated tax certificate. From 6 April 2027, a charge will also apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares ISA. The ISA guide explains this.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Regular income is paid on the 25th of the month to your verified bank account. You can take it monthly, quarterly or annually from a general investment account or ISA.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

The smallest monthly direct debit you can set up is £250. Regular contributions are invested in line with your agreed portfolio on the next dealing day after we receive them.

More details are on the Cash and dealing page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Fund sales are placed at the fund's next valuation point and settle within four working days. Money from a sale can be paid out once settlement has taken place. For shares, trades settle one working day after dealing.

If you also want the money withdrawn to your bank, the documents say a withdrawal is paid within five working days of settlement when holdings had to be sold first. I can't see your specific trade, so I can't give you an exact date.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

The annual exempt amount for capital gains tax is £3,000 for investments sold in a general investment account. Gains above that on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income.

Losses can be set against gains in the same year. They can also be carried forward if you report them to HMRC. Gains inside an ISA or pension are free of UK capital gains tax. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

For advice on your own situation, I can pass you to an adviser.

Outside an ISA, the first £500 of dividends a year is tax-free (the dividend allowance). Above that, dividends are taxed at these rates:
- Basic-rate taxpayers: 10.75%
- Higher-rate taxpayers: 35.75%
- Additional-rate taxpayers: 39.35%

This covers the 2026/27 tax year. It is general information, not personal advice. You can read more in the tax guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

The consolidated tax certificate is published to the portal by the end of May each year. It shows dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

No, we don't complete tax returns. Your adviser can introduce you to an accountant if you need one.

We do provide documents to help with your return:
- A consolidated tax certificate, published to the portal by the end of May each year. It shows dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year.
- A capital gains report. It shows realised gains and losses and the figures needed for the capital gains pages of a tax return.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

A Bed and ISA means selling holdings in a general investment account and buying them back within an ISA. It uses your ISA allowance, and it may realise a capital gain.

On our model portfolios, there is no dealing charge for a Bed and ISA. The documents I found don't say what it costs on anything other than model portfolios. Your adviser can tell you that.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Pension transfers typically take four to eight weeks. The receiving provider starts the transfer. Its scheme carries out the checks required by the pension transfer regulations. It may require you to take guidance from MoneyHelper if those checks raise an amber flag.

We keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

More detail is on the Closing or Transferring page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The new provider starts the transfer. Once we receive their request, we process it.

Use the new provider's transfer process. Don't withdraw the money yourself, because that is how you keep the ISA's tax status. HMRC guidelines say cash ISA transfers should take no more than 15 working days. Other ISA transfers should take no more than 30 calendar days. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

Yes. Your documents stay available in the portal for seven years after the account closes. You can also request paper copies at any time at no charge.

More detail is on the Closing or transferring page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

**Discretionary management:** You agree an investment mandate and a risk level with us. Our investment managers then make the day-to-day decisions within that mandate.

**Advisory management:** We recommend changes, and you decide whether to make each one.

Which one suits you depends on how involved you want to be in individual decisions. Your adviser will discuss both with you, and the choice is recorded in your suitability report. More detail is on the investment management page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Portfolios are managed to one of seven risk profiles. Profile 1 is the lowest risk, mainly cash and short-dated bonds. Profile 7 is the highest risk, almost entirely equities.

You agree your profile with your adviser. This uses a questionnaire and a conversation about your capacity for loss. It is reviewed at every annual review. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

If you have a discretionary portfolio and its value falls by 10% or more since the start of a quarterly reporting period, we tell you by the end of the working day on which it happens.

You also get a quarterly valuation report on the client portal. It is published within 15 working days of each quarter end. The documents don't say how this applies to other types of account. Your investment manager can discuss that with you.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

No. Our independent custodian holds your investments through its nominee company, and legal title is registered in the nominee's name. You remain the beneficial owner.

Your holdings are identified to you in the custodian's records. They are kept separate from the firm's and the custodian's own assets under the Financial Conduct Authority's client assets rules. If the firm or the custodian failed and there were a shortfall, the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may cover eligible claims up to £85,000 per person.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Yes. Each risk profile comes in a responsible version. It excludes companies that get more than 10% of their revenue from tobacco, controversial weapons or thermal coal. It also applies our published responsible investment policy when funds are selected.

Fees are the same as for the standard portfolios. These portfolios don't carry a sustainability label under the FCA's Sustainability Disclosure Requirements. The Responsible Investment Policy is available on request and on the website: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

If you want to know whether this option suits you, that's a question for an adviser.

Yes, Fernhill Wealth is covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS).

- **Investment business:** If we were unable to meet our obligations, eligible clients could claim up to £85,000 per person.
- **Cash:** Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

The FSCS website has more details. More information is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/about-us/

Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

Separately, if Fernhill Wealth couldn't meet its obligations, eligible clients could claim up to £85,000 per person for investment business under the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS). Details are on the FSCS website.

Your cash is held as client money in pooled client bank accounts with our partner banks. It is kept separate from the firm's own money.

We have six offices: Bristol (head office), London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Leeds and Birmingham. Advisers at every office are also available for telephone and video meetings.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Yes. Fernhill Wealth is a trading name of Fernhill Wealth Limited, which is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. You can check our authorisation on the Financial Services Register at register.fca.org.uk.

Fernhill Wealth Limited is registered in England and Wales. Its registered office is Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY.

Fernhill Wealth gives independent advice. We consider products from across the whole market and are not restricted to any provider's range.

More detail is on our financial planning page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/

There are two kinds of first meeting, depending on where you are.

**Introductory meeting:** This is free and has no obligation. It lasts about 45 minutes. It can be at any of our six offices, by telephone or by video call. We explain how we work, what our services cost, and whether we think we can help. You don't need to bring anything. If we both decide to go ahead, we send a client agreement setting out the agreed work and fees before anything is charged. To book, use the Book an Appointment page or call 0808 157 0450.

**Discovery meeting (financial planning):** This is the first step of the planning service. We gather information about your circumstances, goals and attitude to risk. It usually lasts 90 minutes. It helps to bring recent statements for any pensions, investments, mortgages and insurance policies. It also helps to have an idea of your income and regular outgoings. Please never bring or send passwords or PINs.

The written plan is presented at a second meeting. That meeting is usually three to four weeks after your discovery meeting.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/
